title: Chinese Stocks Turn Biggest Losers as Global AI Trade Stumbles
source_used: Bloomberg (read on The Business Times copy)
key_facts: Bloomberg, 17 Oct: the Star50 index, a Nasdaq-style board of Chinese tech firms, has fallen nearly 40% in the current half year, the world's worst-performing major tech gauge.
The ChiNext index has lost 36%; chipmakers MetaX and Moore Threads have each lost about half their value.
The Star50 rose about 75% between April and June and traded at over 80 times forward earnings on 30 June; it now trades at over 40 times, against under 5 for Korea's Kospi and 21 for the Nasdaq 100.

Estimated outflows from the Hong Kong trading link for foreign investors in Chinese local shares were 90 billion yuan (US$13.5 billion) in the third quarter, the biggest in a year (Bloomberg Intelligence).
Equities are the default source of funding for China's AI firms, according to Leonid Mironov, portfolio manager at Gavekal Capital.
Chinese firms have raised US$37 billion from onshore IPOs this year; memory chip maker CXMT is down 27% from its post-listing peak.
Financial regulators met on Thursday 15 Oct and called on state-backed funds, the 'national team', to speed up stock purchases.
quote_evidence: Chinese firms have emerged as the biggest losers of the faltering global artificial intelligence trade, a setback for Beijing's efforts to use stock markets to supercharge its ambition of technological supremacy.
The Nasdaq-style Star50 Index has tumbled nearly 40 per cent in the current half year, becoming the world's worst-performing major tech gauge.
Equities are "the default source" of funding for China's AI firms, according to Mironov.
why_it_matters_hint: Chinese AI firms depend on stock sales for money, so a long slump could slow their funding.
